text:
Riley V: Quick sync on the compact pool card: decide on surge vs burst wording, keyboard flow, and where the SLO guardrail sits. Need a small copy + a11y checklist before handoff.
Ana C: My vote: call it "surge" in UI, but keep "burst_quanta" internal. Surge feels clearer to product folks.
Ben H: Visual treatment: baseline min/max as solid inputs. Surge as a collapsed row with a dashed border when expanded. That keeps it visually separate.
Priya S: Accessibility: the surge toggle must be a real button with aria-expanded. When it expands, set focus to the surge numeric input and announce "surge controls expanded" via live region.
Evan M: Small screens: tooltips for the SLO guardrail currently overlap cost. Proposal: anchor guardrail tooltip below the slider and add a tiny chevron so it doesn't cover numbers.
Riley V: Good. Copy suggestions: header: "Capacity"; min label: "Min GPUs"; max label: "Max GPUs"; surge CTA: "Add surge capacity"; surge pill: "+{n} surge (temporary)"; guardrail short: "SLO guardrail: caps autoscale to meet latency targets. Learn more."
Ana C: Also add a faint "preemptible" chip after pool name when applicable. Make it read-only and include title: "This pool uses preemptible instances".
Ben H: Dev note: don't show internal quanta values. Convert to GPUs server-side and show human units. API fields: `min_capacity`,`max_capacity`,`surge_capacity`,`surge_ttl_seconds`.
Priya S: A11y checklist (copy-paste strings): "aria-labels for min and max inputs", "surge toggle has aria-expanded and aria-controls", "focus moves to surge input on expand", "tooltip anchors below slider on narrow widths", "chips include title attribute and hidden readable text"
Evan M: UX nit: change the guardrail label to just "SLO guardrail" unless it's pre-GA, then append "(beta)".
Riley V: Thanks — I'll update the figma frames and create a tiny prototype for keyboard flow. Ping me if anything else pops up.
A11yBot: Reminder: a11y checklist at https://go/redwood/a11y-checklist (auto-message)
